editorial.headline: Electronic Parts Wholesale: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but foreign investors cannot register it in Bali today.
editorial.body:
KBLI 46521 covers wholesale trade in electronic valves and tubes, semiconductor equipment, microchips, integrated circuits (ICs), and printed circuit boards (PCBs). It is an activity defined by the trade of the components that sit inside electronic systems: the parts through which hardware is assembled, supplied, and moved through commercial channels. The scope is specific, encompassing these listed electronic parts and equipment rather than a general catch-all for every kind of technology-related commerce.

The activity is open across the full stated business-scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code does not reserve its commercial scope for one end of the market. A business registering under it may operate at any of those stated scales, provided its activity remains within the wholesale trade described by the code. The practical question is therefore not whether the category can accommodate a smaller or larger enterprise, but whether the proposed operation genuinely concerns the listed electronic components and equipment.

At the national level, the foreign-investment position is direct. The code is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain terms, a foreign investor may hold the entire company nationally for this activity. The applicable source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no need to soften that national position: the record places this code in the open category and states the full foreign-ownership ceiling.

Bali is the decisive qualification. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, bringing the activity within Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The local status is Blocked (risk class), and the record identifies the moratorium as applying from 13 May 2026. The national permission to hold up to 100% foreign ownership remains real; it simply does not overcome Bali’s current block on PMA registration for this activity.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, this activity permits 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, PMA registration is blocked today.
